title: Meta and Reliance to Build India's First AI Data Centre in Jamnagar, Marking a New Chapter in the $13 Billion Race
excerpt: The 168 MW facility in Gujarat deepens the Zuckerberg-Ambani alliance and positions India as a serious contender in the global AI infrastructure buildout
body:
Meta Platforms and Reliance Industries have announced a landmark partnership to build India's first built-to-suit AI data centre, a 168-megawatt facility in Jamnagar, Gujarat, that will be delivered within two years with options to scale further.

The deal, announced on Wednesday, gives Meta leased capacity at a hyperscale facility that Reliance will design, construct, and operate end-to-end — from renewable power supply and network connectivity to cooling systems using desalinated seawater. Meta will cover the full cost of energy and water supporting operations at the site.

## Why Jamnagar

The choice of Jamnagar is strategic on multiple fronts. The coastal Gujarat city is home to Reliance's flagship energy complex — including the world's largest single-site oil refinery — and offers ready access to power, water, and infrastructure at lower cost than India's major metros. Crucially, the location provides proximity to India's western submarine cable landing stations and Reliance Jio's extensive fibre network.

The facility will also integrate with Meta's Project Waterworth, the world's longest subsea cable system, ensuring high-speed, low-latency data transmission across the region. Reliance can draw energy from its own renewable-power assets in the Jamnagar complex, reducing dependence on costlier grid power.

"This partnership with Meta marks a transformative moment for India's digital infrastructure," said Mukesh Ambani, chairman and managing director of Reliance Industries. "Jamnagar will become a landmark destination for hyperscale AI computing."

Mark Zuckerberg, Meta's CEO, said the "world-class facility in Jamnagar will help us scale our AI infrastructure globally while deepening our long-term investment in India's economy."

## A Relationship Worth Billions

The data centre deal deepens a partnership that has grown steadily since Meta invested $5.7 billion in Jio Platforms in 2020, one of the largest foreign investments in Indian tech history. The companies subsequently formed a $100 million joint venture to develop enterprise AI solutions using Meta's Llama models for Indian businesses and overseas markets.

Moving into physical infrastructure marks a significant escalation. While the financial terms of the new deal were not disclosed, the scope — a 168 MW facility with expansion options, powered entirely by renewables — suggests a multi-billion-dollar commitment when fully built out.

## India's Data Centre Arms Race

The announcement arrives amid a surge in hyperscale data centre construction across India. Amazon, Microsoft, and Google are all building or expanding facilities as New Delhi aggressively courts AI investment. The Indian government has offered foreign companies a more than 20-year tax break on using local data centres, and the country's data centre market is projected to nearly double to $13.11 billion by 2034, according to consulting firm IMARC Group.

The scale of ambition is staggering. In February, Reliance committed approximately $110 billion in investments to position India as an AI hub, while rival Adani outlined $100 billion in parallel investments. Meta's entry into India's physical AI infrastructure adds another powerful player to what is becoming one of the world's most competitive data centre markets.

Separately, Meta announced it has contracted nearly 1 GW of new renewable energy capacity in India through agreements with CleanMax (837 MW of solar and wind projects) and Fourth Partner Energy (88 MW), underscoring the company's commitment to powering its Indian operations sustainably.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For the millions of Indians abroad who rely on Meta's platforms daily — WhatsApp for family calls, Instagram for cultural connection, Facebook for community groups — the Jamnagar data centre could translate into faster, more reliable services across the subcontinent. The facility will support Meta's core business operations alongside its AI computing requirements, potentially improving latency for the 500 million-plus Indians on its platforms.

More broadly, the deal signals that India is no longer just a consumer market for global tech — it is becoming an infrastructure provider. That shift creates high-skill jobs in data centre engineering, renewable energy, and AI operations, adding another dimension to India's already booming tech employment landscape and giving NRI professionals considering a return one more reason to look homeward.
